# Overview

This file summarizes the simulation scripts, saved result files, and plotting scripts used for the simulation figures in the manuscript "Efficient Semi-supervised Frechet Regression with Low-dimensional Manifold Structures".

The first sections check the saved CSV files in `simulation/results/`. Commands for rerunning the experiments are listed near the end of the file.

# Directory setup

Knit this file from the root of the reproducibility folder, the same folder that contains `Readme.md`, `simulation/`, and `real data/`.

```{r directories}
root_dir <- normalizePath(".", winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
sim_code <- file.path(root_dir, "simulation", "code")
sim_plot <- file.path(root_dir, "simulation", "plot")
sim_results <- file.path(root_dir, "simulation", "results")

stopifnot(
  dir.exists(sim_code),
  dir.exists(sim_plot),
  dir.exists(sim_results)
)

data.frame(
  component = c("simulation code", "simulation plot scripts", "saved simulation results"),
  path = c(sim_code, sim_plot, sim_results)
)
```

# Package requirements

The result-file checks below use base R only. Running the simulation and plotting scripts may require the following packages:

- Core computation: `parallel`, `pbapply`, `igraph`, `Matrix`, `matrixStats`.
- SPD response simulations: `shapes`, `RiemBase`, `tmvtnorm`.
- Spherical response simulations: `Directional`, `Riemann`, `spherepc`, `tmvtnorm`.
- Radius experiments: `FNN`, `pracma`.
- Plotting: `ggplot2`, `scatterplot3d`.

# Saved result inventory

Saved CSV files in `simulation/results/`:

```{r saved-simulation-results}
simulation_csv <- sort(list.files(sim_results, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = FALSE))
data.frame(file = simulation_csv)
```

# Visual verification: figures regenerated from saved CSV files

The four panels below are regenerated directly from the saved CSV files and are displayed when this document is knitted. They reproduce Figure 4(a)--(d) in the manuscript and cover the four plotting workflows: graph-radius sensitivity, empirical convergence rate, the no-manifold setting, and comparison with oracle procedures. The time-consuming simulations are not rerun in this section.

```{r visual-verification-setup}
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Package 'ggplot2' is required for the visual-verification figures.")
}
library(ggplot2)

visual_verification_files <- c(
  "Figure 4(a)" = "spd-200-3000-1000-Swiss2-setting1_snr_2_r_impaction.csv",
  "Figure 4(b)" = "spd-1200-3000-1000-Swiss2-setting4-snr_2_rate.csv",
  "Figure 4(c)" = "spd-200-8000-1000-Swiss5-setting3-snr_2.csv",
  "Figure 4(d)" = "spd-100-8000-1000-Curve-snr_2.csv"
)

visual_verification_paths <- file.path(
  sim_results,
  unname(visual_verification_files)
)
missing_visual_files <- visual_verification_files[
  !file.exists(visual_verification_paths)
]
if (length(missing_visual_files) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing saved result files: ",
    paste(unname(missing_visual_files), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

data.frame(
  figure = names(visual_verification_files),
  saved_result = unname(visual_verification_files),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

The following helpers read a named result file and apply the plotting style used by the manuscript scripts. The input filename is explicit so that the document does not depend on editing a hard-coded filename or changing the working directory.

```{r visual-verification-helpers}
read_simulation_result <- function(csv_file, expected_rows, minimum_columns) {
  result_path <- file.path(sim_results, csv_file)
  result <- as.matrix(read.csv(result_path))
  storage.mode(result) <- "double"

  if (nrow(result) != expected_rows || ncol(result) < minimum_columns) {
    stop(
      sprintf(
        "Unexpected dimensions for %s: found %d rows and %d columns.",
        csv_file, nrow(result), ncol(result)
      )
    )
  }
  result
}

make_simulation_line_plot <- function(
    csv_file,
    methods,
    method_levels,
    samples,
    value_columns,
    colors,
    x_label,
    y_limits = NULL,
    legend_position = c(0.99, 0.5),
    legend_justification = c("right", "center")) {
  result <- read_simulation_result(
    csv_file,
    expected_rows = length(samples),
    minimum_columns = max(value_columns)
  )

  plot_data <- data.frame(
    Method = rep(methods, each = length(samples)),
    Samples = rep(samples, times = length(methods)),
    Testing_Error = as.vector(result[, value_columns, drop = FALSE])
  )
  plot_data$Method <- factor(plot_data$Method, levels = method_levels)

  figure <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = factor(Samples),
      y = Testing_Error,
      color = Method,
      group = Method
    )
  ) +
    geom_line(size = 1.2) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 20) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = "Testing error") +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(
        color = "grey80",
        size = 0.5,
        linetype = "dashed"
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.8),
      legend.position = legend_position,
      legend.justification = legend_justification,
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "grey80"),
      legend.key = element_rect(fill = NA)
    ) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(title = NULL))

  if (!is.null(y_limits)) {
    figure <- figure + coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits)
  }
  figure
}
```

## Figure 4(a): graph-radius sensitivity

This panel is regenerated from `spd-200-3000-1000-Swiss2-setting1_snr_2_r_impaction.csv`.

```{r reproduce-figure-4a, fig.width=9, fig.height=6, fig.align="center", out.width="85%", fig.cap="Reproduced Figure 4(a): effect of graph radius on the testing errors of semi-kNN and semi-NW."}
figure_4a <- make_simulation_line_plot(
  csv_file = visual_verification_files[["Figure 4(a)"]],
  methods = c("semi-knn", "semi-nw"),
  method_levels = c("semi-nw", "semi-knn"),
  samples = seq(0.5, 2, 0.1),
  value_columns = 2:3,
  colors = c("semi-knn" = "#66a61e", "semi-nw" = "#e6ab02"),
  x_label = expression("Graph radius (" * "×" ~ r[0] * ")"),
  legend_position = c(0.99, 0.98),
  legend_justification = c("right", "top")
)
figure_4a
```

## Figure 4(b): empirical convergence rate

The saved rate file stores semi-kNN in column `V1` and semi-NW in column `V2`. The manuscript panel uses semi-kNN, so the chunk below explicitly selects `V1`. Dashed lines connect the observed values, and the solid line is a theoretical reference with slope $-0.387$. The fitted empirical slope and $R^2$ are reported separately.

```{r reproduce-figure-4b, fig.width=9, fig.height=6, fig.align="center", out.width="85%", fig.cap="Reproduced Figure 4(b): observed log(AMSE) values connected by dashed lines and a solid theoretical reference line with slope -0.387 for the semi-kNN estimator."}
rate_result <- read_simulation_result(
  visual_verification_files[["Figure 4(b)"]],
  expected_rows = 8,
  minimum_columns = 3
)
rate_sample_sizes <- seq(500, 1200, 100)
rate_x <- log(rate_sample_sizes)
rate_y <- log(rate_result[, 2])
rate_model <- lm(rate_y ~ rate_x)

old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mar = c(5, 6, 4, 2) + 0.1)
plot(
  rate_x,
  rate_y,
  type = "o",
  lty = 2,
  lwd = 2.7,
  col = "#66a61e",
  pch = 16,
  xlab = "ln(n)",
  ylab = "ln(AMSE)",
  cex.lab = 1.8,
  cex.axis = 1.2,
  col.main = "black",
  col.lab = "black",
  col.axis = "black",
  bg = "white"
)
rate_slope <- -0.387
abline(a = mean(rate_y) - rate_slope * mean(rate_x),
       b = rate_slope, col = "#66a61e", lwd = 2.7, lty = 1)
grid(col = "grey80", lty = c(8, 4), lwd = 0.8)
box(col = "black", lwd = 1)
par(old_par)

data.frame(
  method = "semi-knn",
  fitted_slope = unname(coef(rate_model)[2]),
  r_squared = summary(rate_model)$r.squared
)
```

## Figure 4(c): covariates without a low-dimensional manifold structure

This panel is regenerated from `spd-200-8000-1000-Swiss5-setting3-snr_2.csv`. Unlike the standard four-method result files, this CSV stores the two naive-method means in `V1` and `V2` and the two semi-supervised means used in the manuscript panel in `V5` and `V6`.

```{r reproduce-figure-4c, fig.width=9, fig.height=6, fig.align="center", out.width="85%", fig.cap="Reproduced Figure 4(c): testing errors when the covariates do not have a low-dimensional manifold structure."}
figure_4c <- make_simulation_line_plot(
  csv_file = visual_verification_files[["Figure 4(c)"]],
  methods = c("naive-knn", "naive-nw", "semi-knn", "semi-nw"),
  method_levels = c("naive-nw", "naive-knn", "semi-nw", "semi-knn"),
  samples = c(0, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000, 7000, 8000),
  value_columns = c(2, 3, 6, 7),
  colors = c(
    "naive-knn" = "#7570b3",
    "naive-nw" = "#e41a1c",
    "semi-knn" = "#66a61e",
    "semi-nw" = "#e6ab02"
  ),
  x_label = "Unlabeled sample size",
  y_limits = c(0.7, 1.1)
)
figure_4c
```

## Optional standalone figure exports

The original scripts in `simulation/plot/` can still be used to create standalone figure files. These commands are not evaluated while knitting because the scripts write output files and some contain a hard-coded input filename that must first be set to the desired CSV file.

```{r export-standalone-simulation-plots, eval=FALSE}
old_dir <- getwd()
setwd(sim_results)

# plot_main.R: line charts for Figures 2, 3, S.1-S.4, S.9, S.10, S.12, and S.13.
source(file.path(sim_plot, "plot_main.R"))

# plot_radius.R: graph-radius curves for Figure 4(a) and Figure S.5.
source(file.path(sim_plot, "plot_radius.R"))

# plot_rate.R: log(AMSE)-log(n) curves for Figure 4(b) and Figures S.6-S.8.
source(file.path(sim_plot, "plot_rate.R"))

# plot_curve.R: oracle-comparison curves for Figure 4(d) and Figure S.11.
source(file.path(sim_plot, "plot_curve.R"))

setwd(old_dir)
```

# Rerunning simulations

The following chunks are set to `eval=FALSE` because the simulations are relatively time-consuming. Before running them, check the parameter settings listed in the tables above and in the header of each script.

```{r rerun-main-spd, eval=FALSE}
old_dir <- getwd()
setwd(sim_code)

# main_spd.R runs the log-Euclidean SPD simulations for Figures 2, 3, 4(c),
# S.1(a), S.2(a), and S.9.
source("main_spd.R")

# For Figure S.3 (Swiss) or S.4 (Swiss2), run source("main_spd_logcholesky.R") instead.
setwd(old_dir)
```

```{r rerun-main-sphere, eval=FALSE}
old_dir <- getwd()
setwd(sim_code)

# main_sphere.R runs the spherical-response simulations:
# Figures S.1(b), S.2(b), S.10, S.12, and S.13.
source("main_sphere.R")

setwd(old_dir)
```

```{r rerun-radius-experiments, eval=FALSE}
old_dir <- getwd()
setwd(sim_code)

# radius_spd.R runs the SPD graph-radius experiment for Figure 4(a) and Figure S.5(a).
source("radius_spd.R")

# radius_sphere.R runs the spherical graph-radius experiment for Figure S.5(b).
source("radius_sphere.R")

setwd(old_dir)
```

```{r rerun-rate-experiments, eval=FALSE}
old_dir <- getwd()
setwd(sim_code)

# rate_spd.R runs the SPD empirical-rate experiments for Figure 4(b) and Figures S.6 and S.8.
source("rate_spd.R")

# rate_sphere.R runs the spherical empirical-rate experiment for Figure S.7.
source("rate_sphere.R")

setwd(old_dir)
```

```{r rerun-curve-experiments, eval=FALSE}
old_dir <- getwd()
setwd(sim_code)

# curve_spd.R runs the SPD oracle-comparison experiment for Figure 4(d) and Figure S.11(a).
source("curve_spd.R")

# curve_sphere.R runs the spherical oracle-comparison experiment for Figure S.11(b).
source("curve_sphere.R")

setwd(old_dir)
```
